title: HTTP client stack
issueTitle: HTTP client stack for BotTools: suspend transport, outbound-URL guard, response cache, call budget and test fakes
function: BotTools needs a suspend HTTP stack: a transport, an outbound-URL guard, a response cache, a call budget and test fakes. gap.summary: No HTTP stack exists. `Connector` is the only HTTP client: a blocking, stateful line reader over `URLConnection` that sets the JVM-wide `http.agent` on every connect and calls `Unirest.setTimeouts(0, 0)` in its `init`. Nothing offers a suspend request, a typed failure model or a transport port.

options.name: Open failure hierarchy in `kotlin.Result`, builders over `internal` constructors, one opt-in marker through `@SubclassOptInRequired`
options.why: Adding a failure leaf or a builder property never breaks a consumer's compiled code, and the supplied defaults are usable without opting in.

options.name: A sealed failure root, or enums for library-produced reasons
options.why: Each added leaf or entry is a compile error in a consumer's exhaustive `when` and a runtime `NoWhenBranchMatchedException` in a compiled one.

options.name: Flat constructors with defaulted parameters plus hidden deprecated overloads
options.why: A permanent overload per addition kept correct by hand; `@IntroducedAt` is Kotlin 2.3+.

options.name: `kotlin.time.Clock`/`Instant` or kotlinx-datetime in signatures
options.why: An error-level opt-in on every 2.2.x consumer, and the budget needs no calendar arithmetic.

options.name: `fun interface` for `WallClock`
options.why: A `fun interface` cannot carry the subclass gate; one rule for every seam.

options.name: An opaque `Scheduling` type in place of `CoroutineDispatcher`, keeping coroutines `implementation`
options.why: A consumer could no longer pass its own dispatcher, and the coroutines runtime is part of what a suspend API is.

options.name: kotlin-logging in `commonMain`
options.why: A startup line and a runtime dependency on every consumer, with no gain on one published target; an `internal expect fun` seam is the smallest thing that logs.

options.name: A published `js` target instead of check-only modules
options.why: A coordinate and a klib nothing consumes, Node and Yarn downloads for tests, and a published surface the requirements do not name.
options.wins: The day a non-JVM consumer exists.

options.name: KGP's built-in `abiValidation` instead of BCV
options.why: Experimental on 2.2.0 and its DSL changed by 2.4.

options.name: A closed `Trusted`/`Untrusted` pair checked in three layers: pre-check, resolver guard, socket factory
options.why: Every layer alone leaks (measured on 39 host forms); together the socket factory backstops the resolver guard.

options.name: A resolver guard only, or a network interceptor or `EventListener` as the guard
